title: Hospitality supervisor
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Hospitality Supervisors lead teams in housekeeping, food and beverage, or guest services, working in venues across the hospitality industry.
occupationalSummary: <p>Hospitality supervisors work across a wide variety of businesses including bars, restaurants, cafés, conference centres, banqueting venues, hotels, cruise ships, hospitals or contract caterers. They provide vital support to management teams and are capable of independently supervising hospitality services and running shifts. They typically work under pressure, leading a team to deliver fantastic customer service&nbsp; The majority of hospitality supervisors’ skills and knowledge are the same but supervisors typically specialise one of the four occupations in this standard.&nbsp;</p>

knowledges.detail: Methods to support, motivate, and monitor team to deliver high quality guest service.
Techniques used to supervise others to meet business standards relevant to role
Standard business operating procedures and how to support consistent use in a team
Standards for communication with guests and colleagues
Principles of supervising and training teams to maintain a safe, clean working environment; record keeping, modelling good practice
Health and safety legislation, regulations, guidelines and procedures relevant to own self and team
Functions and procedures for safe and correct use of equipment and technology used by team including fault prevention.
Company procedures for fixing or escalating equipment or technology faults and contingency plans in case of equipment or technology failure
Principles of managing communication during team briefings, instructions and difficult conversations with the team.
Task prioritisation and allocation techniques to meet demand
Techniques for monitoring and reporting on team performance, supporting improvements where necessary
Procedures and methods for resolving guest feedback or complaints
Techniques for briefing or training team on new products or processes
Performance criteria and feedback techniques to support team to meet performance expectations
Methods to sustainably reduce the waste of resources in line with business expectations
Techniques to ensure the fair and respectful treatment of all team members, and ensure equity diversity and inclusion legislation is followed
Key performance indicators, and own responsibility for team meeting their expected contribution to KPIs, in terms of efficiency, performance, and profitability
Principles of coaching and training
Techniques to tackle inappropriate behaviour, conflict or underperformance in team
Techniques to tackle inappropriate behaviour from or conflict with customers
Legislation, regulation, and policies related to guest privacy and safety including fire safety, emergency evacuation, data protection, child protection, and modern slavery.
